questions.question: Which of the following describes a luminous object?
options: An object that absorbs all light hitting it
An object that gives out its own light
An object that reflects light from other sources
An object that lets light pass through it

questions.question: How does a mirror-like surface reflect light compared to other, rougher surfaces?
options: It absorbs light instead of reflecting it
It scatters light in all directions
It reflects light in a regular way
It bends light as it passes through

questions.question: Through which part of the eye does light enter, and where is it detected?
options: Enters through the retina and is detected by the pupil
Enters through the pupil and is detected by the retina
Enters through the iris and is detected by the lens
Enters through the cornea and is detected by the optic nerve

questions.question: Under what condition can a beam of light traveling through the air be seen?
options: Only if the light hits something and reflects or scatters towards an eye
Only if the light is travelling in a complete vacuum
Only if the light beam is extremely narrow
Only if the light has a very high frequency

questions.question: What is an echo?
options: A sound that travels faster than the speed of light
A sound heard again after reflecting off a hard surface and travelling back
A sound that is absorbed completely by a soft material
A sound that has its frequency increased by a barrier

questions.question: Why do soft surfaces absorb a large amount of sound?
options: They reflect the sound waves in a single direction
They increase the speed of the sound waves
The sound waves transfer energy by making the particles in them vibrate
They contain a vacuum which prevents sound from travelling

questions.question: In light reflection diagrams, what is the 'normal'?
options: A line drawn parallel to the reflecting surface
An imaginary line drawn at 90 degrees to the point of reflection
The actual path that the incoming light ray takes
The angle between the mirror and the reflected ray

questions.question: If a ray of light hits a flat mirror with an angle of incidence of 35 degrees, what is the angle of reflection?
options: 55 degrees, on the same side of the normal
35 degrees, on the other side of the normal
90 degrees, along the normal line
145 degrees, on the other side of the normal

questions.question: Where does the reflection of an object in a flat mirror appear to be located?
options: Slightly closer to the mirror than the actual object is
Directly opposite the object, at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front
Twice as far behind the mirror as the object is in front
Right on the surface of the mirror glass

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the image seen in a flat mirror?
options: It is upside down and laterally inverted
It is the right way up and laterally inverted
It is upside down and not laterally inverted
It is the right way up and not laterally inverted

questions.question: Which statement best describes how light travels?
options: In straight lines at an extremely high speed, spreading out as it travels
In curved lines at a relatively slow speed, staying in a tight beam
In straight lines at the same speed as sound, without spreading
In waves that require a solid medium to travel through

questions.question: What is a shadow?
options: An area of bright light focused by a lens
A reflection of an object on a rough surface
An unlit area in the shape of an object that is blocking light
The path of light as it bends around a transparent obstacle

questions.question: How does the amplitude of a sound vibration affect what we hear?
options: A greater amplitude results in a higher pitch
A greater amplitude results in a louder sound
A greater amplitude results in a quieter sound
A greater amplitude results in a lower pitch

questions.question: What is frequency in relation to sound, and how does it affect pitch?
options: It measures the size of a vibration; greater frequency means a louder sound
It measures how often vibrations occur; greater frequency means a higher pitch
It measures how far a sound travels; greater frequency means a lower pitch
It measures the speed of particles; greater frequency means a quieter sound

questions.question: Why does sound travel fastest through solids?
options: Because solid particles are very far apart and do not collide
Because solids have no attractive forces between their particles
Due to strong attractive forces between particles, so many vibrate when one does
Because sound waves are converted into light waves inside solids

questions.question: Why is it impossible for sound to travel through a vacuum?
options: A vacuum absorbs all vibrations and turns them into light
Sound waves are too fast to be contained in a vacuum
Sound waves are caused by particle vibrations, and a vacuum has no particles
The temperature of a vacuum is too low for sound to travel

questions.question: Which of the following is true about how sound travels through the air?
options: Air particles travel all the way from the sound source to the listener's ear
The pattern of vibrating particles creates a sound wave, but the air particles do not travel along with it
Sound waves travel by shifting vacuum gaps between the air particles
Air particles are permanently pushed away from the source and never bounce back
